name: Fresh Green
lede: Fresh Green is a bright, clean green from the xkcd 2010 color-naming survey, echoing a phrase writers have long used for lively plant color, including an elephant's suit.

sections.title: A modifier on green, with an older phrase
sections.body: Fresh Green pairs "fresh" with [[green]], the xkcd 2010 survey's term for this bright, clean green [1]. The exact compound is the survey's; the phrase is older. Pastoureau notes that the elephant Babar has worn "a lovely, fresh green" suit since his first storybook appearance, so enduringly that the shade is sometimes called "Babar green" [2]. He adds that Belle Époque public gardens favored a "delicate or fresh green" for plantings, against duller, greyer greens for benches and gates [3]. Its nearest named look-alikes are [[apple]], [[apple]] and [[vibrant-green]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive shows this color covering at least one percent of its canvas, within CIEDE2000 4 of it, as photographed [4]. In printed English, the phrase "fresh green" rose fastest in the 1840s and peaked around 1870, though that tracks every sense of the words, not just this color name [4].
